blocks.en: 1. The Question Behind This Course
blocks.es_reference: 1. La Pregunta Detrás de Este Curso

blocks.en: Somewhere this morning a believer opened a Bible. Not an original manuscript — no one has those — but a translation of a copy of a copy, printed and bound and carried to church in his own hands. And a fair question sits under that worn cover: can I trust the Bible I actually hold? This course takes that question seriously and answers it honestly. We are, as the old phrase has it, a people of the book — and a people of the book ought to be able to say why. Luke felt the same weight. He tells Theophilus he wrote "an orderly account... that you may know the certainty of those things in which you were instructed" (Luke 1:3–4). Notice the goal: not doubt, not endless suspense, but certainty — the settled confidence of a person who has looked into the matter. That is the posture of this whole course. We will examine the evidence the way Luke examined his — carefully, honestly, without fear — and we will arrive where he arrived: at certainty about the Word of God.
blocks.es_reference: Esta mañana, en algún lugar, un creyente abrió una Biblia. No un manuscrito original — nadie los tiene — sino una traducción de una copia de una copia, impresa y encuadernada, llevada a la iglesia en sus propias manos. Y bajo esa gastada cubierta yace una pregunta justa: ¿puedo confiar en la Biblia que en verdad tengo? Este curso toma en serio esa pregunta y la responde con honestidad. Somos, como dice la antigua frase, un pueblo del libro — y un pueblo del libro debería poder decir por qué. Lucas sintió el mismo peso. Le dice a Teófilo que escribió "por orden... para que conozcas la certeza de las cosas en las cuales has sido enseñado" (Lucas 1:3–4). Nota la meta: no la duda, no la suspensión interminable, sino la certeza — la confianza asentada de quien ha examinado el asunto. Esa es la postura de todo este curso. Examinaremos la evidencia como Lucas examinó la suya — con cuidado, con honestidad, sin temor — y llegaremos adonde él llegó: a la certeza acerca de la Palabra de Dios.

blocks.en: 2. Where Our Certainty Rests
blocks.es_reference: 2. Dónde Descansa Nuestra Certeza

blocks.en: Before we weigh a single piece of evidence, we must be clear about what our confidence actually rests on — because it is easy to get this backward. Our certainty does not rest on archaeology, or on manuscripts, or on our success at answering every hard question. It rests on this: Scripture is the inspired, God-breathed Word of God.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de pesar una sola prueba, debemos tener claro sobre qué descansa realmente nuestra confianza — porque es fácil invertir el orden. Nuestra certeza no descansa en la arqueología, ni en los manuscritos, ni en nuestro éxito al responder toda pregunta difícil. Descansa en esto: la Escritura es la Palabra inspirada, exhalada por Dios.

blocks.en: "All Scripture is given by inspiration of God" (2 Timothy 3:16). "Holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit" (2 Peter 1:21).
blocks.es_reference: "Toda la Escritura es dada por inspiración de Dios" (2 Timoteo 3:16). "Los santos hombres de Dios hablaron siendo inspirados por el Espíritu Santo" (2 Pedro 1:21).

blocks.en: That is the foundation, and we confess it — we do not hold it in suspense, waiting for a spade to turn it up. The evidence in this course strengthens our confidence; it never becomes the ground of it. A believer's trust finally rests on the character of the God who spoke, and on the witness of His Spirit — not on the next excavation. Keep that order straight and everything else falls into place. Lose it, and you have made the perfect Bible into the one you are still waiting to prove.
blocks.es_reference: Ese es el fundamento, y lo confesamos — no lo tenemos en suspenso, esperando que una pala lo saque a la luz. La evidencia de este curso fortalece nuestra confianza; nunca llega a ser su fundamento. La confianza del creyente descansa finalmente en el carácter del Dios que habló y en el testimonio de su Espíritu — no en la próxima excavación. Mantén ese orden y todo lo demás cae en su lugar. Piérdelo, y habrás convertido la Biblia perfecta en la que todavía esperas probar.

blocks.en: 3. Absolute Authority: The Bible in Your Hand
blocks.es_reference: 3. Autoridad Absoluta: La Biblia en Tu Mano

blocks.en: A throne — not a fortress to defend inch by inch.
blocks.es_reference: Un trono — no una fortaleza que defender palmo a palmo.

blocks.en: So how do we speak of what this book is? Not first as a fortress to be defended inch by inch, but as a throne. Scripture carries the absolute authority of God Himself. It commands. It binds the conscience. It settles the question. It stands over every human authority and answers to none. "Thus says the LORD" was never an argument; it was a verdict. And notice what Jesus did with Scripture — He did not defend its accuracy, He wielded its authority: "It is written." "Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away" (Matthew 24:35). Here is the part that matters most for you: this authority rests on the Bible you are actually holding — in your own language, in your own hands — not on a lost original you must take on faith. The apostles preached with full authority from a translation, the Greek Old Testament, and never paused to defend a pristine autograph. The authority travelled into the copy. It always has. The Word of God comes to you now, in the book on your lap, and it comes with the right to be obeyed.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo, entonces, hablamos de lo que es este libro? No primero como una fortaleza que defender palmo a palmo, sino como un trono. La Escritura lleva la autoridad absoluta de Dios mismo. Ordena. Obliga la conciencia. Zanja la cuestión. Se levanta sobre toda autoridad humana y no responde ante ninguna. "Así dice Jehová" nunca fue un argumento; fue un veredicto. Y observa lo que Jesús hizo con la Escritura — no defendió su exactitud, empuñó su autoridad: "Escrito está." "El cielo y la tierra pasarán, mas mis palabras no pasarán" (Mateo 24:35). Aquí está lo que más importa para ti: esta autoridad descansa en la Biblia que en verdad tienes — en tu propio idioma, en tus propias manos — no en un original perdido que debes aceptar por fe. Los apóstoles predicaron con plena autoridad desde una traducción, el Antiguo Testamento griego, y jamás se detuvieron a defender un autógrafo intacto. La autoridad pasó a la copia. Siempre lo ha hecho. La Palabra de Dios viene a ti ahora, en el libro sobre tu regazo, y viene con el derecho de ser obedecida.

blocks.en: 4. Revelation and Inspiration: Content and Process
blocks.es_reference: 4. Revelación e Inspiración: Contenido y Proceso

blocks.en: Two words get confused constantly, and keeping them apart clears up much. Revelation is about content — it is God disclosing what we could never have reasoned our way to. Some of that disclosure is general, given to everyone: "His invisible attributes are clearly seen... even His eternal power and Godhead" (Romans 1:20), so that no one is without excuse. And some is special: God's direct word through the prophets, through Scripture, and finally through His Son. Inspiration is a different thing — it is about process, how God moved human authors to write that word down. It helps to remember that the Word of God comes in more than one form: the Living Word, who is Christ (John 1:1); the preached and prophetic Word; the natural Word of creation; the written Word, the Bible; and the enacted Word of baptism and the Lord's Supper. This course concerns the written Word — but the written Word points to all the others, and above all to the Living One. We are a people of the book because the book gives us the Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Dos palabras se confunden constantemente, y distinguirlas aclara mucho. La revelación trata del contenido — es Dios revelando lo que jamás habríamos razonado. Parte de esa revelación es general, dada a todos: "las cosas invisibles de él... su eterno poder y Deidad" (Romanos 1:20) se ven claramente, de modo que nadie tiene excusa. Y parte es especial: la palabra directa de Dios por los profetas, por la Escritura y, finalmente, por su Hijo. La inspiración es otra cosa — trata del proceso, de cómo Dios movió a autores humanos para escribir esa palabra. Ayuda recordar que la Palabra de Dios viene en más de una forma: la Palabra Viva, que es Cristo (Juan 1:1); la Palabra predicada y profética; la Palabra natural de la creación; la Palabra escrita, la Biblia; y la Palabra representada del bautismo y la Cena del Señor. Este curso trata de la Palabra escrita — pero la Palabra escrita apunta a todas las demás, y sobre todo al Viviente. Somos un pueblo del libro porque el libro nos da al Cristo.

blocks.en: 5. How the Word Was Breathed: The Dynamic View
blocks.es_reference: 5. Cómo Fue Exhalada la Palabra: La Visión Dinámica

blocks.en: How exactly did God "breathe out" Scripture through men? Four answers have been offered. The dictation theory says God dictated every word, the writers merely taking it down. The natural theory says they were inspired only as any great author is — a Shakespeare with a soul. The partial theory says only some parts are truly inspired. Each of these fails the evidence of the text itself. The best answer is the dynamic view: God's Spirit so guided the writers that what they wrote was exactly His Word, yet He worked through their full humanity — their personality, their vocabulary, their research, their tears. The Bible is therefore a Divine/Human book. And that should sound familiar, for it is the same pattern we meet in Christ Himself, who is fully divine and fully human, and in preaching, which is a divine message through a human voice. This is the deep reason we can trust it in every part: because it is God-breathed, it is true in all that it affirms — not because we have answered every alleged discrepancy, but because the God who spoke it does not lie.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo exactamente "exhaló" Dios la Escritura por medio de hombres? Se han ofrecido cuatro respuestas. La teoría del dictado dice que Dios dictó cada palabra, y los escritores solo la anotaron. La teoría natural dice que fueron inspirados solo como cualquier gran autor — un Shakespeare con alma. La teoría parcial dice que solo algunas partes son verdaderamente inspiradas. Cada una falla ante la evidencia del texto mismo. La mejor respuesta es la visión dinámica: el Espíritu de Dios guió a los escritores de tal modo que lo que escribieron fue exactamente su Palabra, y sin embargo obró por medio de su plena humanidad — su personalidad, su vocabulario, su investigación, sus lágrimas. La Biblia es, por tanto, un libro Divino/Humano. Y eso debería sonar familiar, pues es el mismo patrón que hallamos en Cristo mismo, plenamente divino y plenamente humano, y en la predicación, un mensaje divino por una voz humana. Esta es la razón profunda por la que podemos confiar en ella en cada parte: porque es exhalada por Dios, es verdadera en todo lo que afirma — no porque hayamos respondido cada supuesta discrepancia, sino porque el Dios que la habló no miente.

blocks.en: 6. The Rules of Evidence
blocks.es_reference: 6. Las Reglas de la Evidencia

blocks.en: Now to the tools. When we bring evidence to bear on Scripture, we must be honest about what evidence can and cannot do, because three different things get lumped together under one word. The first is proof — evidence so complete it settles a matter beyond dispute. In history, real proof is rare; we almost never get it. The second is corroboration — evidence that confirms and supports, that makes a claim credible and lines up with it, without slamming the door on every alternative. This is the honest workhorse; it is what the witnesses in this course mostly supply. The third is illustration — evidence that makes the real vivid, that lets you see the world of the text with your own eyes. Archaeology, for example, corroborates and illustrates far more often than it ever "proves." None of this weakens our case. It strengthens it, because a claim honestly labelled is a claim that holds. The trouble begins only when we confuse the three — when we call corroboration "proof" and then cannot deliver.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora, a las herramientas. Cuando traemos evidencia sobre la Escritura, debemos ser honestos sobre lo que la evidencia puede y no puede hacer, porque tres cosas distintas se agrupan bajo una sola palabra. La primera es la prueba — evidencia tan completa que zanja un asunto sin disputa. En la historia, la prueba real es rara; casi nunca la obtenemos. La segunda es la corroboración — evidencia que confirma y apoya, que hace creíble una afirmación y concuerda con ella, sin cerrar la puerta a toda alternativa. Es la herramienta honesta; es lo que en su mayoría aportan los testigos de este curso. La tercera es la ilustración — evidencia que hace vívido lo real, que te deja ver el mundo del texto con tus propios ojos. La arqueología, por ejemplo, corrobora e ilustra mucho más a menudo de lo que jamás "prueba". Nada de esto debilita nuestro caso. Lo fortalece, porque una afirmación honestamente rotulada es una afirmación que se sostiene. El problema empieza solo cuando confundimos las tres — cuando llamamos "prueba" a la corroboración y luego no podemos entregarla.

blocks.en: 7. Two Ways to Go Wrong: The Camel and the Gnat
blocks.es_reference: 7. Dos Maneras de Errar: El Camello y el Mosquito

blocks.en: Jesus once rebuked men who "strain out a gnat and swallow a camel" (Matthew 23:24) — meticulous about the tiny thing, careless about the huge one. In matters of biblical evidence there are two ways to go wrong, and they are exactly that pair. The skeptic swallows a camel: he takes an assumption dressed up as a finding — a scholar's guess, a claim repeated so often it feels like fact — and swallows it whole without ever checking it. You hear it in one confident sentence: "The Bible is full of errors and contradictions." Yet ask for a single instance — one real error, one true contradiction — and often the reply is silence, for the speaker has never examined the evidence to reach that verdict; he is passing on what he heard, from someone who very likely passed it on too. A conclusion reached that way rests on feeling, not on evidence weighed — which is the very charge the skeptic levels at the believer. The honest path is the same for both: produce the example, and weigh it. Where a genuine difficulty is raised we will not wave it off but look at it squarely, as this course does throughout; what we refuse is to swallow the slogan whole. Whole doctrines have been built on such unexamined claims, some carried faithfully for fifty years because a trusted teacher said so. The believer makes the opposite mistake: he strains at gnats and overclaims, insisting "archaeology proves the Bible," "there are no real difficulties." That sounds like faith but it manufactures fragility — for the student told that, who then meets an honest dispute, can lose more faith than the doubt was ever worth. This course refuses both. We concede what is genuinely open, we refuse what is merely assumed, and we stand without apology where the faith is settled. Even a cherished claim must be tested; that testing is not weakness but honesty.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús una vez reprendió a hombres que "cuelan el mosquito, y tragan el camello" (Mateo 23:24) — minuciosos con lo diminuto, descuidados con lo enorme. En materia de evidencia bíblica hay dos maneras de errar, y son exactamente ese par. El escéptico traga un camello: toma una suposición disfrazada de hallazgo — una conjetura de un erudito, una afirmación tan repetida que parece un hecho — y la traga entera sin comprobarla jamás. Lo oyes en una sola frase confiada: "La Biblia está llena de errores y contradicciones". Pero pide un solo caso — un error real, una verdadera contradicción — y a menudo la respuesta es el silencio, pues quien lo dice nunca examinó la evidencia para llegar a ese veredicto; está repitiendo lo que oyó, de alguien que muy probablemente también lo repitió. Una conclusión alcanzada así descansa en el sentimiento, no en evidencia sopesada — que es precisamente la acusación que el escéptico lanza contra el creyente. El camino honesto es el mismo para ambos: presenta el ejemplo, y sopésalo. Donde se plantea una dificultad genuina no la descartamos, sino que la miramos de frente, como este curso hace en todas partes; lo que rechazamos es tragar la frase entera. Doctrinas enteras se han levantado sobre tales afirmaciones no examinadas, algunas sostenidas fielmente por cincuenta años porque un maestro de confianza lo dijo. El creyente comete el error opuesto: cuela mosquitos y exagera, insistiendo en que "la arqueología prueba la Biblia", "no hay dificultades reales". Eso suena a fe, pero fabrica fragilidad — pues el estudiante al que se le dijo eso, y que luego halla una disputa honesta, puede perder más fe de la que la duda jamás valió. Este curso rechaza ambos. Concedemos lo que verdaderamente está abierto, rechazamos lo que solo se supone, y nos mantenemos sin disculpa donde la fe está establecida. Aun una afirmación querida debe probarse; esa prueba no es debilidad, sino honestidad.

blocks.en: 8. Four Witnesses to a Trustworthy Bible
blocks.es_reference: 8. Cuatro Testigos de una Biblia Confiable

blocks.en: Everything ahead is organized around a single question — can we trust the Bible we hold? — and four witnesses that answer it. The first witness gives us the right books: the canon, how these Scriptures came to be recognized. The second gives us the right words: the text, its transmission down the centuries, and its preservation. The third gives us real events: archaeology, the world behind the text shown to be solid ground. The fourth gives us the real stage: geography, the places where it all happened. No single witness carries the whole weight, and none needs to; together they form a cord not easily broken. And they let us make an honest promise to the believer with the worn Bible in his hands. We do not say, "Trust me, the lost originals were flawless." We say: God so preserved His Word through all the copying and the translating that what you hold is His authoritative Word — and you may rest under it. Let us call the first witness.
blocks.es_reference: Todo lo que sigue está organizado en torno a una sola pregunta — ¿podemos confiar en la Biblia que tenemos? — y a cuatro testigos que la responden. El primer testigo nos da los libros correctos: el canon, cómo estas Escrituras llegaron a ser reconocidas. El segundo nos da las palabras correctas: el texto, su transmisión a través de los siglos y su preservación. El tercero nos da los hechos reales: la arqueología, el mundo detrás del texto mostrado como terreno firme. El cuarto nos da el escenario real: la geografía, los lugares donde todo sucedió. Ningún testigo por sí solo lleva todo el peso, y ninguno lo necesita; juntos forman un cordón que no se rompe fácilmente. Y nos permiten hacer una promesa honesta al creyente con la Biblia gastada en sus manos. No decimos: "Confía en mí, los originales perdidos eran perfectos." Decimos: Dios preservó su Palabra de tal modo, a través de toda la copia y la traducción, que lo que tienes es su Palabra con autoridad — y puedes descansar bajo ella. Llamemos al primer testigo.

sa.prompt: State the question this course sets out to answer, and explain why it matters to an ordinary believer.
sa.model: The course asks whether we can trust the Bible we actually hold — a translation of a copy, not an original. It matters because ordinary believers stake their lives on this book and deserve to know, with certainty, that what they hold is God's reliable Word.

sa.prompt: On what does a believer's certainty ultimately rest, and what does evidence do?
sa.model: Certainty rests on the fact that Scripture is the inspired, God-breathed Word — on the character of the God who spoke and the witness of His Spirit — not on evidence. Evidence strengthens our confidence; it never becomes the ground of it.

sa.prompt: Explain why the course prefers to speak of Scripture's "absolute authority," and how that authority reaches the Bible in the believer's hand.
sa.model: Absolute authority is a positive claim: Scripture commands, binds the conscience, and stands over us — a throne, not a fortress to defend. That authority rests on the Bible the believer holds, because authority travels into the copy, just as the apostles preached with full authority from a translation.

Revelation is about content — God disclosing what we could not have reasoned to, whether general (creation, conscience) or special (Scripture, Christ). Inspiration is about process — how God moved human authors to write that word down accurately.

sa.prompt: Describe the dynamic view of inspiration and the analogy the unit draws to it.
sa.model: The dynamic view holds that God's Spirit so guided the writers that what they wrote was His Word, yet He worked through their full humanity — personality, vocabulary, research. The Bible is thus a Divine/Human book, like Christ who is fully divine and fully human, and like preaching.

sa.prompt: Name and define the three things evidence can do.
sa.model: Proof settles a matter beyond dispute, and in history it is rare. Corroboration confirms and supports a claim without closing every alternative — the honest workhorse. Illustration makes the real vivid, letting us see the world of the text.

sa.prompt: Explain what the unit means by the skeptic's "camel," using the idea of an unexamined claim.
sa.model: The camel is an assumption dressed up as a finding — a scholar's guess or a claim repeated so often it feels like fact, swallowed whole without checking. Whole doctrines have rested on such unexamined claims, carried for decades because a trusted teacher said so.

sa.prompt: Explain the apologist's "gnat-strain" and why overclaiming is dangerous.
sa.model: The gnat-strain is overclaiming — insisting "archaeology proves the Bible" or "there are no real difficulties." It sounds like faith but manufactures fragility, because a believer told that who later meets an honest dispute can lose more faith than the doubt was ever worth.

sa.prompt: State the threefold discipline this course adopts toward evidence.
sa.model: We concede what is genuinely open, we refuse what is merely assumed, and we stand without apology where the faith is settled. Even a cherished claim must be tested; that testing is honesty, not weakness.

sa.prompt: Name the four witnesses of the course and state the honest promise they let us make to the believer.
sa.model: The four witnesses are the canon (right books), the text and its transmission and preservation (right words), archaeology (real events), and geography (real stage). Together they let us tell the believer honestly: not "trust me, the lost originals were flawless," but "God so preserved His Word that what you hold is His authoritative Word."
